newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Asian Dev Bank agrees $60 mln project loan to PNG.
newsitem.headline: Asian Dev Bank agrees $60 mln project loan to PNG.

text.p: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) said on Friday it had approved $60 million in loans to finance the Health Sector Development Programme of Papua New Guinea (PNG).
The programme aims to improve the quality and accessibility of health care especially among women and children in remote rural areas, an ADB statement said.

"The programme...will emphasise capacity-building in the nation's health care agencies, health centres and posts and closer collaboration with churches, non-governmental organisations and private health services," it said.
The Manila-based, multilateral financing institution said $45 million will come from its ordinary capital resources, which carry a maturity of 25 years including a five-year grace period.
The interest rate will be determined by the bank's pool-based variable lending rate.
The remaining $15 million in loans will be from its interest-free Asian Development Fund, which has a maturity of 35 years including a 10-year grace period.
PNG has one of the worst disease incidence and health status indicators in the region, the ADB noted.
